newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says aims to cut taxes when sensible.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says aims to cut taxes when sensible.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he aimed to cut taxes when it was sensible to do so.
In a series of radio and television interviews from the Conservative party conference in Bournemouth, he described himself as "an enthusiastic tax-cutter."
"People trust us only to cut taxes when we can sensibly afford to do so," Clarke said.
People paid less tax when Conservatives were in government for any length of time but tax cuts had to be justified and credible and good for the economy, he added.
"We are going to win the election," Clarke said.

"We do dare, as we have shown, to take extremely tough action when we have to to make sure that now I'm able to start cutting taxes, as I did last November, and cutting taxes in future whenever, but only whenever, it's sensible to do so, giving the stable conditions to our industry and our commerce."
Clarke said the vast majority of Conservative delegates agreed that tax-cutting was "a very good thing for Conservative governments to do."
But the government had to keep public finances healthy and meet its obligations on education, health and the police.
"Last year I managed to cut taxes. Maybe not every year. The longer you have a Conservative government, the more those taxes will come down," Clarke added.
"If you go back to New Labour, then you'll find taxes will soon enough start going up. They always do."
The Chancellor said the "feelgood factor" was returning and he predicted that this would win the election for the government.
